newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore reforming margins swing back into profit.
newsitem.headline: Singapore reforming margins swing back into profit.

text.p: Singapore refiners are cautiously increasing reforming runs after margins turned positive for the first time in six months, industry sources said on Wednesday.
Since July last year reforming margins have been below the critical $4.00-per-barrel mark, a margin needed to ensure production of gasoline is profitable on the basis of 95-octane product.

Singapore prices for naphtha, the feedstock for the reformer units which produce reformate, a gasoline blendstock, is almost $6.00 per barrel below 95-octane gasoline prices -- showing a positive margin for refiners.
"It only moved above $2.00 last week, and at this sort of spread, if it continues, we will produce more," a trader at a Singapore refinery told Reuters.
The positive margins fell to below $2.00 in August when a glut of gasoline hit the markets with the increase in refining capacity in Thailand and South Korea.

Over the last six months, Singapore refiners cut their 127,900 barrel-per-day (bpd) reforming output as low as 70 percent, effectively running at a loss but maintaining production because of the need to produce hydrogen -- a by-product of reforming which is used in other secondary refining units.
One refiner said it was now running its reformers at 80-percent, but was not confident about increasing production further until it was more convinced the naphtha/gasoline spread could be maintained.
"We are thinking about it but have not quite decided because the numbers have been pushed," a trader with a major oil company said. "The question is whether it (the spread) can be sustained."

Another source said his refinery was quick to boost its reformers to full capacity to take advantage of the re-emergence of profits, which he expected to "last until the end of March with Indonesian shutdowns."

Indonesia plans to purchase up to half a million barrels of gasoline in March because of the scheduled 38-day shutdown of the 120,000-bpd Dumai refinery and techincal problems at Balongan's 83,000-bpd hydrocracker, which is affecting output at the 125,000-bpd refinery.
